items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1969-06-17
items.q: So me Wilford, George James, three of us played in the room.

ctx.x: Yeah. T. Rouch, or no, no, I mean not him. Bikes. And that boy would do Rodney, that boy plays. He was playing. Then I had with the chorus playing, you know, he play with Fat Domino now. He used to play guitar. He played bass with Fat Domino. Little short fella. Oh I know, Jimmy Davis. Yeah, Jim. From up to Carrollton. Yeah, little Jim. Little Jim played with us a long time. And then on his rope rope. He told me that you told me. Yeah, on his rope rope, playing with me there. You know what I mean? But I'll tell…

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1962-11-01
items.q: That's George James' nephew. Oh yeah, I remember him.

ctx.x: Tell us the name of some of them. Some of your favorite walls, do you know? Or you can hum them, whichever you want to do. Well. Well, I know you play the walls I saved for you, that's what I mean. Why don't you say it for me? Yeah, walls I saved for me, down by the middle of the street, and, uh,

I wonder who's kissing her now, and, uh, and, uh, oh, so many of them. I know, sure. So many of them. And, uh, so, well, I tell you, in fact, when you play for, when we stand up at the Moose, you have to play waltzes, you see? You have to play waltzes, cause a lot of people love waltzes. You play, we play so many, so many, we play maybe one or two slow ones, one or two fast ones, then maybe every side or maybe something like that, or the fourth waltz like that, you see? For the people, cause they love the…
That's what I want. I know. It's right what you say. I've noticed. You know, you don't come tell them right.
